featured_reviews.name: Naomi Barton
featured_reviews.review_text:
This is an aesthetic clinic masquerading as a medical dermatologist now in a shamefully bad way that seems to be exclusively to make as much money as possible.

Very sad to see the drop in standards. Three years ago I visited for a hormonal acne complaint and had a wonderful doctor who swiftly prescribed me the necessary and low cost medication that was appropriate after conducting a proper investigation.

I took my friend here this time for a complaint and was told by the doctor that the only way to address an inflammatory autoimmune condition is homeopathy. HOMEOPATHY IS NOT MEDICINE. The doctor failed to disclose that she is not qualified under any actual medical guidelines, but only as a homeopath.

She tried to prescribe oral Tretinoin and accompanied it with a number of actives in a manner completely inappropriate to the skin condition - which was flaky and peeling rash that is either dermatitis or psoriasis. We had to insist on refusing and she did not disclose the side effects. After pushing her on other meds based on consultationsn with other doctors she then prescribed basic medication Topisal (300 bucks!!) that is actually appropriate to the condition.

She added a whole bunch of other stuff that was completely unnecessary. We have just used Topisal + Nivea Creme (Blue tin) and it has resolved everything overnight.

I am horrified that this clinic, which used to be a gold standard that I would recommend to all my friends. I would also seriously warn anyone who is using these services to first check on whether the person prescribing you medical procedures is actually qualified to do those - just because our healthcare governance and regulation has gone to the dogs doesn't mean that these charlatans are actual medical professionals, and you should protect yourselves.

Understanding the Language of Natural Hairlines

A natural hairline is not a single line — it is a layered design built from frontal points, a soft transition zone, a core density zone, and direction that follows your own hair pattern. The height, shape, and graft distribution should suit your face shape today and remain appropriate as your hair loss pattern evolves over the years.

The transition zone at the very front uses single-hair grafts to blend the hairline softly into the forehead
The frontal points and their height determine whether the result reads as youthful or mature
Temporal recess should be supported gently — overfilling creates a blocky, unnatural frame
Hair caliber, curl, and skin tone contrast all affect how much density is needed for a natural look
Donor management — reserving grafts for future crown or mid-scalp work — is as important as the hairline itself

You've been losing hair for months. You start minoxidil 5%, but after six months, results plateau. Your dermatologist mentions 10%. But is stronger really better? The answer might surprise you- it could save you money and side effects.

Hair loss affects millions of people worldwide, and minoxidil remains one of the most clinically validated topical treatments available. However, confusion persists about whether higher concentrations deliver better results. This comprehensive guide compares minoxidil 5% and 10%, examining clinical evidence, side effects, and practical considerations to help you make an informed decision.

A biotin IV infusion for hair growth pushes concentrated Vitamin B7 directly into your bloodstream. By bypassing the digestive tract, a biotin IV drip for hair ensures 100% bioavailability, accelerating keratin synthesis and strengthening the hair shaft from within.

While traditional oral supplements are effective for general maintenance, intravenous therapy is a clinically superior option for individuals with malabsorption issues, chronic stress-induced shedding, or documented deficiencies. Most patients observe a visible improvement in hair density and texture within 8 to 12 weeks of consistent clinical sessions.

If you have been taking daily biotin supplements for months with no visible change in hair density, you are not alone. It is a common frustration among many young to middle-aged people to see visible thinning in spite of taking biotin gummies.

At Kibo Clinics, we frequently address the fact that vitamins sometimes fail because the gut absorbs only a limited amount of nutrients. While oral tablets are the standard starting point, a biotin IV drip for hair is a clinical alternative that bypasses digestive barriers.

Both treatments support keratin production, but they interact differently with your biology. One depends on digestion, while the other delivers nutrients directly to the bloodstream. This guide explains how a biotin IV drip works, what nutrients it contains, and who benefits the most.

Hair Transplant Graft Calculator. This tool helps you understand your approximate graft needs.

Every hair transplant is different. The number of grafts you need depends on where you have lost hair, how dense your donor area is, and what kind of coverage will look natural on your scalp. This is why hair transplants are planned around graft numbers rather than fixed packages.

A graft is a naturally occurring unit of hair follicles. Each graft usually contains between one and four hairs. During a transplant, these grafts are taken from the donor area (usually the back and sides of the head) and placed into thinning or balding areas.

Your total graft requirement is what determines how much coverage can be created and how your final hairline and density will look.

India or Turkey - where should you really get your hair transplant done?

Turkey became popular for all-inclusive medical tourism packages. India, on the other hand, is leading with doctor-led, personalised treatments using advanced techniques like Sapphire FUE and Body Hair Transplant (BHT).

According to global hair restoration reports, many poor outcomes overseas are linked to unlicensed clinics. In India, the focus stays on surgeon involvement, aftercare, and long-term results, not just the procedure day.

If you’re choosing between cost, safety, and natural outcomes, make sure you consult a qualified hair transplant doctor first.

First Visit Cost: Rs. 500/- (Consulting Fee) + Rs. 1,500/- (First Payment) = Rs. 2,000/- paid.
